headline: High-risk default interaction: n8n can write server files and call APIs while RD-Agent uploads to external LLM/Kaggle services, creating leakage and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and orchestrate tools; RD-Agent can run browsers and consume files/logs. If n8n passes RD-Agent-generated content through shared files or workflow nodes, attacker-controlled text could be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF n8n writes RD-Agent output into a shared file or workflow variable that later drives tool calls
IF RD-Agent ingests n8n-produced text as instructions without provenance tagging
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in workflow outputs
Store agent outputs in separate directories
Require human review before any tool-call step
Strip executable markup from inter-agent messages
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all handoffs

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n handles server filesystem data and per-credential secrets, while RD-Agent sends data to OpenAI/Azure OpenAI/DeepSeek/Kaggle APIs. If the same workflow processes sensitive files, n8n can expose them to RD-Agent’s outbound API calls, creating exfiltration risk by default unless the operator isolates data flows.
conditions: IF the workflow processes secrets, financial reports, or other sensitive files
IF RD-Agent is configured to send those inputs to external APIs
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workflows
Disable external API steps for sensitive jobs
Use redaction before handoff to RD-Agent
Restrict n8n file access to a dedicated directory
requires-engineering: enforce data-class routing policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and n8n can write the server filesystem while RD-Agent writes logs. Their concurrency models allow multiple instances, so simultaneous runs can collide on shared files or shared downstream services. The profiles do not show locking, so conflict is plausible in default multi-run setups.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or log directory
IF multiple instances run concurrently against the same downstream API quota or file path
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Use per-run log filenames
Limit concurrent instances during shared-resource jobs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can orchestrate actions from AI Agent nodes, and RD-Agent produces research outputs, logs, and execution traces that may be treated as authoritative. If n8n consumes RD-Agent output without verification, erroneous research claims can cascade into automated workflow actions. The pair therefore has a direct default path from generated content to action-taking.
conditions: IF n8n uses RD-Agent output as an input to downstream workflow nodes
IF no verification step checks RD-Agent claims before action execution
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any action node
Require citations or source links for claims
Route outputs to a review queue first
Disable auto-commit or auto-send steps
requires-engineering: add schema validation for agent outputs

E_compliance.rationale: n8n handles per-credential secrets and arbitrary workflow data, while RD-Agent explicitly touches financial reports and competition datasets and sends data to third-party APIs. That creates a likely retention/residency mismatch if regulated or contractual data is routed through RD-Agent’s external services. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or contractual data is processed by the shared workflow
IF retention or deletion obligations apply to data sent through RD-Agent APIs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of RD-Agent workflows
Document retention settings for each external API
Minimize logged fields in n8n and RD-Agent
Review vendor DPAs before enabling sensitive datasets
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
